title: Geography
description: Geography (H.C.G. Paper 2) for ICSE Examination Year 2027: topographical map work, the outline map of India and the geography of India.

syllabusBaselines.source: CISCE, ICSE Regulations and Syllabuses, Examination Year 2027 - Geography (H.C.G. Paper 2); corroborated by the Educart and Jagran Josh 2026-27 syllabus reproductions.
syllabusBaselines.note: Verified October 2026. Part I is map work (interpretation of Survey of India topographical sheets and the outline map of India); Part II is the geography of India in nine units. 80-mark 2-hour paper, 20 marks internal assessment; one project report is required.

sections.title: Part I: Map Work
sections.description: Reading a Survey of India topographical sheet and marking India on an outline map.

chapters.title: Interpretation of Topographical Maps
chapters.blurb: Grid references, contours, conventional symbols, scales, directions, settlement, land use, drainage and transport on a Survey of India sheet.

chapters.title: Map of India
chapters.blurb: Locating, marking and naming the prescribed relief, river, water body, wind, mineral, soil, city and population features on an outline map.

sections.title: Part II: Geography of India
sections.description: The physical and economic geography of India.

chapters.title: Climate
chapters.blurb: Temperature, rainfall and wind patterns, the factors controlling India's climate, the monsoon mechanism and the four seasons.

chapters.title: Soil Resources
chapters.blurb: Alluvial, black, red and laterite soils, soil erosion and conservation.

chapters.title: Natural Vegetation
chapters.blurb: Evergreen, deciduous, desert, littoral and mountain vegetation, and the programmes that conserve Indian forests.

chapters.title: Water Resources
chapters.blurb: Surface and ground water, rainwater harvesting and the methods of irrigation used across India.

chapters.title: Mineral and Energy Resources
chapters.blurb: Iron ore, manganese, copper and bauxite; coal, petroleum and natural gas; hydel power and the non-conventional sources.

chapters.title: Agriculture
chapters.blurb: Indian agriculture and the Green Revolution, farming types, agricultural seasons and the growing of rice, wheat, pulses, sugarcane, oilseeds, cotton, jute and tea.

chapters.title: Manufacturing Industries
chapters.blurb: Classification of industry, sugar and textile manufacturing, iron and steel plants and the petrochemical and electronics industries.

chapters.title: Transport
chapters.blurb: Roadways, railways, airways and waterways with their advantages, disadvantages and the national highway network.

chapters.title: Waste Management
chapters.blurb: The impact of waste, safe disposal, reducing, reusing and recycling, and the global warming and acid rain issues behind it.
